meta_description: High-end kitchen remodeling across Miami-Dade and Broward: custom cabinetry, stone, structural openings, permits pulled and closed. Call (786) 273-2524.
h1: Your kitchen, rebuilt from the block out
hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and real layout changes for high-end kitchens in Miami-Dade and Broward. A licensed general contractor, a fixed written scope, permits pulled and closed, and one supervisor on site every working day.
local_heading: What a kitchen is up against here
intro_paragraphs: A high-end kitchen remodel in South Florida is rarely a facelift. It is the room taken back to block and slab, the layout redrawn, and a cabinet package built to order instead of pulled off a shelf. The owners who call us have already concluded the room is wrong: Merrick-era and mid-century houses whose kitchens were designed as service rooms, 1990s builder houses where a soffit and a peninsula still define the space, and waterfront or condo buyers who intend to gut the kitchen before the furniture arrives. The kitchen is the main room of the house now, and it gets built like it.

What changes here is the envelope and the paperwork. Both counties sit inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so a kitchen that enlarges a window or adds a terrace door carries product-approval documents into plan review, either a Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance or a Florida Product Approval evaluated for the HVHZ. Near the water, flood rules apply: work valued above half the building's value counts as substantial improvement, and materials below base flood elevation have to be flood-resistant. Permitting then splits by county. Miami-Dade cities each run their own building department with county environmental and water-and-sewer approvals still attached, and Broward's cities run theirs under Broward's county amendments; in each county a Board of Rules and Appeals certifies the inspectors and officials who review it.

Before anything is demolished you get a fixed written scope: cabinetry by specification, stone by slab, appliances by model number, and every trade line named. Cabinet fabrication sets the calendar, so the order goes in early and your existing kitchen keeps working while the boxes are built. Final dimensions are taken after demolition rather than off a drawing, stone is templated once the cabinets are standing, and rough inspections are attended in person. Our supervisor is there every working day. At the end the permit is closed out, which is the part that matters when you sell or refinance.

We build kitchens in 42 areas across the two counties, and no two behave alike. In Coral Gables and the Miami Beach historic districts, an interior kitchen goes straight to plan review while anything visible from the street meets a design or historic board first. On Key Biscayne, Fisher Island and in the Brickell towers, the association's alteration agreement sets hours, elevators and insurance before the city ever sees a drawing. Along the Broward waterfront, in Harbor Beach, Rio Vista, the Las Olas isles and Lighthouse Point, flood elevation drives the detailing. West in Weston, Parkland and Coral Springs it is gate logistics and 1990s framing. Pick your area for the local version.
scope_heading: What goes into a PGX kitchen
scope_intro: Every kitchen is priced line by line before demolition starts. These six pieces show up on almost every project we run in Miami-Dade and Broward.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry built to order
scope_items.desc: Cabinet packages drawn to the room as it actually measures after demolition, finished for year-round humidity, and detailed to meet old ceilings and out-of-square walls without apology.

scope_items.name: Stone counters and islands
scope_items.desc: Slabs selected at the yard, templated once the boxes are set, seams placed where the eye does not land, and seated overhangs carried on steel sized for the load.

scope_items.name: Openings, beams and structure
scope_items.desc: Where the wall between kitchen and living room carries load, an engineer sizes the beam and the drawing is signed, sealed and permitted before the first block comes out.

scope_items.name: Plumbing, gas and power
scope_items.desc: Relocated drains and supply lines, dedicated circuits, panel capacity confirmed before an induction range is specified, and gas work permitted and pressure-tested rather than improvised.

scope_items.name: Hoods, ducts and makeup air
scope_items.desc: A hood sized to the range and ducted outdoors where the building allows it, with makeup air where exhaust passes the code threshold and an approved exterior termination.

scope_items.name: Hardware that survives salt air
scope_items.desc: Close to the ocean we specify stainless in the grade that actually resists chlorides, with finishes and sealants chosen for humidity, salt and hard sun rather than for the showroom.

faqs.q: Is a kitchen ever small enough to skip the permit?
faqs.a: Almost certainly. Electrical, plumbing, mechanical, gas and structural work all require permits and inspections in both counties. Florida's HB 803 exemption, in effect since July 1, 2026, lifts the permit requirement for some single-family work valued under $7,500, but it carves out exactly those five trades, does not apply to property in a flood hazard area, and forbids splitting a project to slip under the threshold. A real kitchen touches the excluded list on day one, so we permit it and close it out.

faqs.q: From the first call to the first dinner, how long?
faqs.a: Count in months, in three parts. Design and specification, then permitting, then construction. Custom cabinetry is usually the longest single item on the calendar, months of fabrication that we start early so the old kitchen keeps working. Once demolition begins, a straightforward layout commonly runs a couple of months on site; moving walls, gas, ductwork or the electrical panel extends that, and a condo building's approval process and elevator schedule can add weeks of their own.

faqs.q: How much should we budget for a kitchen at this level?
faqs.a: Cabinetry, stone and appliances set the floor, and all three are chosen rather than fixed, which is why any honest range is wide. What separates two kitchens of the same size is usually invisible: moving waste lines, adding circuits or a panel, cutting a duct through concrete block, engineering an opening. We put a number on it after walking the room and writing the specification, never before. If price alone decides it, we would rather say so at the walk-through than halfway through demolition.

faqs.q: What sends a kitchen back to the drawing board?
faqs.a: Almost always one of four things. A condo board that has not signed off on the alteration agreement, because a city permit does not override a building's rules. An open permit left by a previous owner that surfaces when we apply for ours. A partition that turns out to be bearing, which sends the drawing back to an engineer. And in flood zones, a scope that grows until it crosses the substantial improvement threshold and pulls the whole structure into current code. We check all four before quoting.

faqs.q: Who do I call at four o'clock when something is wrong?
faqs.a: One supervisor, on your job every working day, running our own trade crews instead of a chain of brokered subs. PGX is licensed and insured under Lic. CGC1539072, two decades and more of it in this market, with 150-plus remodels and additions delivered under permit and inspection. The person who walks you through the scope is the one who walks the inspector through the rough-in and hands you the closed permit.

faqs.q: Gas or induction, and can the hood vent outside?
faqs.a: The building usually decides both. Adding or extending a gas line needs its own permit in either county, and where no gas main serves the street the alternative is propane, which brings tank setback rules with it. Above ground level in a tower, propane storage runs into fire-code limits, and plenty of buildings ban gas ranges outright. Induction removes the fuel question but asks more of the panel, so we verify capacity first. Venting depends on whether the building allows a duct through wall or roof.

cta_sub: Walk us through the room, tell us what it gets wrong, and we will measure and put a fixed scope in writing, in English o en español.
